gap: No result ChatGPT got works out what the Creative Pebble Pro costs at its full 30 W RMS once you add the USB-C PD charger that isn't in the box: $66.49 + $23.99 (UGREEN Nexode 65W) = $90.48, or $3.02 per RMS watt. That is $4.51 below the Creative T60 ($94.99 for 30 W RMS with its adapter, $3.17/W), which the first chat showed as the step-up pick. Run off a PC's own USB port, the Pebble Pro costs $6.65 per watt.
standout_why: Stackandvalue (cited) says the Pebble Pro gives 10 W RMS on a USB port and 30 W with a separately sold 30 W PD adapter. It gives $2.17/W at 30 W, but it leaves the adapter's cost out and never compares the Pebble Pro with the T60 on output. Dupple (a result, not cited) lists $/RMS-watt for the T60 ($3.17), Z407 ($3.25) and M60 ($3.03 at $199.99), but it scores the Pebble Pro only at 10 W ($6.65/W) and never mentions the adapter. I couldn't read the body text of Tom's Hardware, TechRadar, Tom's Guide (list page and Pebble Pro review) or PC Gamer: WebFetch returned only their headlines, and my scripted fetch to check them was not approved. Wired blocked fetching. So I can't rule out that one of those pages mentions the adapter, but none of the readable pages works out the cost with it included.
decides: This supports the second chat's 'Pebble Pro for most PCs' pick, as long as the page tells shoppers to add a 30 W+ USB-C PD charger. With the charger, the Pebble Pro matches the T60's 30 W RMS for $4.51 less. Without it, the Pebble Pro runs at a third of its rated power and is the worst value per watt of the 2.0 picks. It also ties in a Dealectric listing (ugreen-nexode-65w-3-port-charger) as the add-on. Both Creative models only list SBC for Bluetooth, so neither has a codec edge for PC use.
